Frequency-bearing reference-period bounds

Source: R/time-range.R
time_range.Rd

time_range() constructs one range from scalar Date or POSIXct endpoints with the same carrier and first_period <= last_period. It preserves the supplied reference-period anchors and datetime timezones without coercion.

Usage

time_range(first_period, last_period, frequency)

as_time_range(x, frequency, ...)

# S3 method for class 'Date'
as_time_range(x, frequency, ...)

# S3 method for class 'POSIXct'
as_time_range(x, frequency, ...)

Arguments

first_period, last_period

Scalar Date or POSIXct reference periods.

frequency

One nonmissing canonical code accepted by frequency_code().

x

A Date or POSIXct vector of reference periods.

...

Reserved for methods; no additional reduction options are used.

Value

A list-backed tosi_time_range with fields frequency (a scalar tosi_frequency_code), first_period and last_period.

Details

as_time_range() reduces a Date or POSIXct vector using min() and max() and calls time_range(). Frequency is explicit; missing times are not filtered and there is no empty-time recovery. Bounds do not imply continuous occupancy, an enumerated domain, calendar alignment or per-series coverage.

Examples

time_range(as.Date("2020-01-01"), as.Date("2022-01-01"), "A")
#> $frequency
#> [1] A
#> 35 Levels: A S Q M W2 W D A2 A3 A4 A5 A10 A20 A30 A_3 M2 M_2 M_3 W3 W4 ... N15
#> 
#> $first_period
#> [1] "2020-01-01"
#> 
#> $last_period
#> [1] "2022-01-01"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "tosi_time_range"
as_time_range(as.Date(c("2022-01-01", "2020-01-01")), "A")
#> $frequency
#> [1] A
#> 35 Levels: A S Q M W2 W D A2 A3 A4 A5 A10 A20 A30 A_3 M2 M_2 M_3 W3 W4 ... N15
#> 
#> $first_period
#> [1] "2020-01-01"
#> 
#> $last_period
#> [1] "2022-01-01"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "tosi_time_range"
